answer: A slow-burn trust ember stops sybil farms. Each identity starts as one ember with 5% voting weight and no payouts. First, it completes one verified task daily for 90 days, each checked by two established peers. Second, weight rises 1% per clean week, reaching full power at day 180. Third, any failed check resets the ember to zero, burning its history. Forging 10,000 fakes then needs 900,000 tasks and $720,000 in compute and oversight over six months, so the fable of cheap bots collapses. Like a raven guarding one nest, the network watches each ember until it proves it can keep burning.
